newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Traders eye term/spot tenders.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Traders eye term/spot tenders.

text.p: Light distillates were steady on Friday amid thin talk as naphtha traders focused on term talks while the gasoline market awaited news on India's buy tender and fresh Indonesian demand, traders said.
"After Taiwan yesterday, the market is really quiet," a gasoline trader said on the lack of fixed price talk on the Singapore fob market.

Traders said the market was bearish on Taiwan's purchase of just one 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded 95-octane reformate at around $24.70 per barrel c-and-f Keelung or Taichung arriving July 16-30 in a tender.
But they said the market was likely to improve with limited exports from South Korea and China amid high domestic demand.
Meanwhile, at least two cargoes were being sought for the Mideast for June delivery and fresh demand from Indonesia was likely to emerge amid refinery turnarounds.
Indonesia's 200,000-bpd Balikpapan refinery will shut for a month's maintenance and the 100,000-bpd Cilacap crude unit closes from August 13 for 35 days.
Traders were also waiting to see how many cargoes India would buy in its tender for 25,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery June 18-22, which is due to be awarded later on Friday.
The spot naphtha market was dull in the absence of firm demand as buyers focused on term talks.
Naphtha June swaps were steady at $21.10/$21.30 per barrel and July at $21.45/$21.60.
One refiner was heard to have sold 100,000-barrels of July naphtha at 60-70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, up from market assessments of 40-70 cents.
But traders said the premium was too high in light of the bearish market.
"There is not much demand in Japan and South Korea and there are a lot of arb cargoes from the Med," a trader said. "But in August it should pick up as the petchem plants start up from turnaround."

But North Asian buyers were currently preoccupied with Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) talks for one-year term supplies of 500,000-700,000 tonnes of naphtha starting in July - due to be finalised soon.
Kuwait Petroleum Corp is to meet buyers in London on Monday to discuss one-year term supplies of two million tonnes of full range naphtha starting in August.
But the Mideast market might be under pressure with Saudi Aramco offering a package of 50,000-tonnes each of A-180 and Jubail monthly from June-September.
Some traders said the cargoes were rumoured offerd over a four month period.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
